title: Function-vector Mirror compression basis
hypothesis: Function vectors extracted as hidden-state deltas from support demonstrations can be compressed into a shared PCA Mirror basis while preserving held-out in-context mapping accuracy, at lower intervention payload bytes than explicit per-task vectors.
physical_object: one frozen GPT-2 LM and one shared layer-6 residual-stream intervention site
mirror_coordinate: task-specific coefficient vector over a development-fitted shared function-vector basis
logical_multiplicity: 8 arbitrary object-to-color mapping tasks per world, with four held-out queries each
controls: explicit full-precision function vector per task

task.type: few-shot arbitrary object-to-color mapping with GPT-2

development.allowed: fit PCA basis from development function vectors only; fixed layer 6 and ranks 4/8/16; no fresh-dependent changes

storage.authority: actual serialized intervention payload bytes; separately charge the exact GPT-2 safetensors checkpoint plus root tokenizer/config files used at inference (not duplicate ONNX/TF/TFLite/Flax exports)
paid_objects: explicit task vectors or shared PCA mean/basis and task coefficients

success_gate: Direct ICL baseline must exceed chance (12.5%) in every fresh world; at least one PCA rank must retain >=90% of explicit-vector accuracy and use <=50% of explicit-vector payload bytes in every fresh world.
failure_gate: Direct ICL baseline is not above chance, explicit function vectors do not improve held-out target accuracy over query-only, or PCA compression loses >10% explicit-vector accuracy / misses the byte gate.
boundaries: Single small GPT-2 checkpoint and synthetic arbitrary word mappings; not a reproduction of GPT-J Function Vectors or a broad NLP benchmark.
Function vectors are extracted from support activations with a fixed contrastive prompt; no model weight updates.
Causal function accuracy, not code combination count, determines usefulness.
